mainTopic: ערכין responsibility and the details of שילוח הקן: where it applies, hints to Purim figures, and why non-kosher birds are exempt
overview: This amud covers several topics. First, the גמרא finishes a ברייתא showing that ערכין money stays the owner's responsibility until it reaches the Temple גזבר, so it restates רב המנונא's words to match. Then it returns to the משנה and brings a ברייתא on the פסוק of שילוח הקן. 'כי יקרא' teaches that you need not search for a nest, and the other words of the פסוק cover kosher birds, private and public places, trees and the ground. The גמרא gives 'לפניך' and 'בדרך' new lessons: birds that ran away from their owner, and a nest found in the sea, but not one in the sky. רב מתנה rules that a nest on a person's head counts, and he finds hints to משה, המן, אסתר and מרדכי in the תורה. The גמרא explains the name of הורדוס's pigeons and tells רב כהנא's story about them. Finally, רבי יצחק learns from the word צפור that a non-kosher bird is exempt, and he defends this against four challenges. Another challenge begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows ערכין money stays the owner's responsibility
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא teaches that ערכין money stays חולין until it reaches the גזבר. This goes against רב המנונא's original statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think ערכין is like the other case, where the owner is not responsible. So the פסוק says 'And he shall give your valuation'. The money stays non-holy, and the owner is still responsible for it, until it reaches the Temple treasurer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it quoted to challenge רב המנונא. The ברייתא says that with ערכין, the owner stays responsible for the money until the גזבר receives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that ערכין might follow the same rule as a case where the owner carries no responsibility. Then it rejects that idea from the פסוק. The money counts as חולין, and stays the owner's responsibility, until it reaches the גזבר. This contradicts רב המנונא's statement as it was first reported.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': it introduces a possible mistake that the פסוק will then correct
'The verse teaches': it introduces the פסוק that settles the question
Pledging to the Temple the fixed 'value' the תורה sets for a person
Non-holy, ordinary property
The Temple treasurer

steps.title: רב המנונא's statement is restated correctly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes what רב המנונא said. Everyone agrees that with ערכין you are responsible even without saying 'עלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רב המנונא said something, this is what he said: Everyone agrees about ערכין that even if a person did not say 'upon me', he is responsible. The פסוק says 'And he shall give your valuation', which means the money stays non-holy in your hand until it reaches the treasurer.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the ברייתא contradicts the old version, the גמרא says רב המנונא must have actually said the opposite. With ערכין, everyone agrees you are responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, being responsible for a pledged item depends on saying 'עלי' ('it is upon me'). ערכין is different: you are responsible even without that word. This now fits the ברייתא exactly, because it is built on the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it was said, this is how it was said': the גמרא's way of correcting how a statement was reported
Everyone agrees: no one disputes this point
'Upon me': wording that takes on personal responsibility for a pledge

steps.whatToRemember: With ערכין, a person stays responsible for the money until it reaches the גזבר, even if he never said 'עלי'.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is arguing with רב המנונא. The גמרא is fixing how his words were reported, and the corrected version says the opposite of the first one.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what does 'כי יקרא' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about stringencies in כסוי הדם. It then brings a ברייתא asking what the words 'כי יקרא קן צפור לפניך' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'There is a stringency in covering the blood, etc.' The Rabbis taught: 'If a bird's nest happens before you'. Why does the פסוק say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. A ברייתא then asks why the פסוק of שילוח הקן uses these words. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said כסוי הדם is stricter in one way, because שילוח הקן applies only to birds that are not readily available. The ברייתא now looks for where that limit comes from in the פסוק's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency: a way one מצוה is stricter than another
The מצוה to cover the blood after slaughtering a wild animal or bird
A bird's nest: the setting for the מצוה of שִׁלּוּחַ הַקֵּן
'Etc.': a sign that only the start of the משנה is being quoted

phrases.english: There is a stringency in covering, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the start of our משנה, which compares covering the blood with sending away the mother bird.

steps.title: You do not have to search for a nest
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק says 'שלח תשלח', you might think you must search for nests. 'כי יקרא' teaches that the מצוה applies only when you happen upon one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'You shall surely send away the mother, and the young you may take for yourself.' So you might think a person must go around mountains and hills to find a nest. That is why the פסוק says 'If it happens': only when it comes up in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The words 'כי יקרא' show that you only do שילוח הקן with a nest you happen to come across. You do not have to go looking for one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong, doubled verb 'שלח תשלח' could make it sound like a duty you must actively go out and fulfill. The words 'כי יקרא' limit the מצוה to a chance meeting. This is where the משנה gets its rule that שילוח הקן applies only to birds that are not readily available.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely send away': the doubled verb of the מצוה of שִׁלּוּחַ הַקֵּן
'If it happens': it shows the מצוה applies when you come across a nest by chance
Something that happens to you by chance
Mountains and hills: places you would have to search

steps.whatToRemember: שילוח הקן is not a מצוה you must go out and look for. It applies only when you happen to come across a nest, as the words 'כי יקרא' teach.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that שילוח הקן is more limited than כסוי הדם. It applies only to a nest you come across, not to birds that are readily available in your home.

phrases.english: Since it is stated:
"You shall surely send away the mother

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי יקרא' teaches that you do not have to search for a nest. The מצוה applies only when you happen to come across one.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns details of the מצוה from each word
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes word by word through the פסוק and learns which nests, which birds, and which places the מצוה covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nest' means any nest. 'Bird' means a kosher bird, not a non-kosher one. 'Before you' means private property. 'On the way' means a public area. How do we know trees count? The פסוק says 'in any tree.' How do we know pits, ditches and caves count? The פסוק says 'or on the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues reading the פסוק of שילוח הקן one word at a time, and each word adds a new detail to the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק has its own job. 'צפור' limits the מצוה to kosher birds. 'לפניך' and 'בדרך' cover private and public places. 'בכל עץ' and 'או על הארץ' stretch it to trees, pits, ditches and caves.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher bird
Non-kosher (here, a non-kosher bird)
Private property
Public area

phrases.english: "Nest" – any nest at all,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. It means any nest counts, even one with a single chick or egg.

phrases.english: "Bird" – a kosher one and not a non-kosher one,
"Before you" – on private property,
"On the way" – in a public area,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every word of the פסוק adds a detail: any nest, only kosher birds, private and public property, trees, and pits, ditches and caves.

steps.title: Why do we need 'before you on the way'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why 'לפניך בדרך' is needed, since the end of the פסוק already includes every place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since in the end we include every place anyway, why do I need 'before you on the way'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices a problem with what it just said, and asks a question. It is setting up a new job for the words 'לפניך בדרך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בכל עץ או על הארץ' already covers every possible place. So listing 'לפניך' and 'בדרך' just to include places seems extra. The ברייתא wants to know what these words really teach.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end we will include
Why do I need it? (this seems extra)

steps.title: Only a nest that is not in your possession
steps.stepSummary: 'בדרך' teaches that the מצוה applies only to a nest that is not in your possession, like a nest on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to tell you: just as a nest on the road is not in your possession, so too the מצוה applies to any nest that is not in your possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. 'On the way' is a model: the מצוה covers nests that are like a nest on the road, which do not belong to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דרך' is no longer just a place. It becomes an example of a kind of nest: one that is not under your control. Any nest like that is included, and a nest that is yours is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (comparing a whole category to one example)
Its nest is not in your possession

phrases.english: To tell you: just as on the road,
its nest is not in your possession,
so too, any case where its nest is not in your possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאֵין קִנּוֹ בְּיָדֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לפניך בדרך' teaches that the מצוה applies only to a nest that is not in your possession.

steps.title: Practical cases: which birds are included and which are exempt
steps.stepSummary: Based on this rule, the חכמים list which birds' nests need שילוח and which are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: dovecote pigeons and attic pigeons that nested in wall holes or buildings, and geese and chickens that nested in an orchard, require sending away the mother. But if they nested inside the house, and also house-raised pigeons, there is no obligation to send.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the rule 'only a nest not in your possession' to real cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Geese and chickens that were once kept at home but escaped and went wild, so they no longer return home, need שילוח when they nest outside, in a place you don't control (Rashi). Birds nesting inside the house, and fully house-raised pigeons, are considered in your possession, so they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a rule taken from what was just learned)
Sending away the mother bird
Dovecote, a home for pigeons
House-raised (domesticated) pigeons

steps.whatToRemember: The מצוה of שילוח הקן applies only to a nest that is not in your possession. Geese and chickens count only if they escaped and went wild and nested somewhere outside your control.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Pigeons of a dovecote and pigeons of an attic

and geese and chickens that nested in an orchard –
one is obligated to send away the mother,
but if they nested inside the house,
and likewise house-raised pigeons –
one is exempt from sending away the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 7 to practical cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds nesting outside your control (including formerly domesticated birds that escaped and went wild) require שילוח; birds nesting inside the house and house-raised pigeons are exempt.

steps.title: We already know this from 'כי יקרא', and 'לפניך' is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the rule about a nest in your possession is already learned from 'כי יקרא', and private property is already included by the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: just as on the road the nest is not in your possession, so too any nest not in your possession. Why do I need this? We already learn it from 'כי יקרא': 'כי יקרא' leaves out a nest that is ready at hand. And also, why do I need 'before you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks back at the ברייתא and attacks its reading of 'לפניך בדרך' with two problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First problem: step 4 already learned from 'כי יקרא' that a nest ready at hand is left out, so 'בדרך' cannot be needed for that. Second problem: 'לפניך' was used for private property, but 'בכל עץ או על הארץ' already covers every place. So both words still seem extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (from a different source)
Leaving out a nest that is ready at hand
And furthermore (a second problem)

phrases.english: The Master said: just as "on the way" –
its nest is not in your possession,
so too any case where its nest is not in your possession.
Why do I need this?
It is learned from "if it happens",

And furthermore, why do I need "before you"?

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'בדרך' for 'not in your possession' and 'לפניך' for private property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both lessons are already learned from other words ('כי יקרא' and 'בכל עץ או על הארץ'), so these words would be extra.

steps.title: 'לפניך' includes birds that ran away from their owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives 'לפניך' a new job: birds that once were in your control and then ran away are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'before you' comes to include birds that were before you and then rebelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second problem by giving the word 'לפניך' a new lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds that once had an owner and were in his hands, and then ran off and nested elsewhere, might seem to still belong to him. 'לפניך' teaches that they still need שילוח.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (a new explanation replacing the old one)
To include
They rebelled, ran away

phrases.english: Rather, "before you"

phrases.notes: He means birds that once had an owner and were in his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about 'לפניך' from step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a new lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לפניך' teaches private property, which is already covered elsewhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לפניך' includes birds that were once in an owner's control and ran away.

steps.title: 'בדרך' includes a nest found in the sea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives 'בדרך' a new job: like רב יהודה in the name of רב, a nest found in the sea is included, since the sea is called a 'way'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On the way' is like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: if one found a nest in the sea, he must send away the mother, as it says: 'So said ה׳, who makes a way in the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first problem by giving 'בדרך' a new lesson, based on a statement of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'כי יקרא' already teaches the 'not in your possession' rule, 'בדרך' is free for something else. A פסוק in ישעיהו calls the sea a 'way,' so 'בדרך' includes a nest found at sea.

keyTerms.meaning: Like what רב יהודה said
He found a nest in the sea
As it says (quoting a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, 'לפניך' includes birds that ran away from their owner, and 'בדרך' includes a nest found in the sea.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of 'בדרך'. The ברייתא used it for 'not in your possession,' but the גמרא now uses it for a nest in the sea, because 'not in your possession' already comes from 'כי יקרא'.

phrases.english: "On the way" – is like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב,
for רב יהודה said in the name of רב:

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בדרך' teaches that the nest must not be in your possession, which is already known from 'כי יקרא'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בדרך' includes a nest found in the sea, since the sea is called a 'way'.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now every word in the פסוק has its own lesson and none is extra, which is how the גמרא expects a פסוק to be read.

steps.title: Should a nest in the sky also count?
steps.stepSummary: If the sea counts as a 'way' because a פסוק calls it that, then the sky should count too, since a פסוק calls it 'the way of an eagle'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, if someone found a nest in the sky (as it says 'the way of an eagle in the sky'), would he also be obligated in שילוח הקן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 11. If a פסוק calling the sea a 'way' is enough, then a nest in the sky should also need שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 used the rule that any place a פסוק calls 'דרך' is included. The גמרא shows a strange result of that rule: the sky is also called 'דרך' in משלי. So either the sky is included too, or the rule needs to be made sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: if your reasoning is right, look at this odd result
The מצוה of sending away the mother bird from the nest
'The way of an eagle': the sky, as described in משלי

phrases.english: But if that is so,

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that any place a פסוק calls 'דרך' counts for שילוח הקן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: the sky is also called 'דרך' in a פסוק, so it would have to be included, which seems wrong.

steps.title: The sky is only 'the way of an eagle', not a plain 'way'
steps.stepSummary: The sky is called 'דרך' only with an added word ('of an eagle'). The sea is called a plain 'דרך'. So only the sea is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sky is called 'the way of an eagle'. It is not called just 'a way'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It makes the rule more exact: only a place called plain 'דרך', with no added words, counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is in the wording of the פסוקים. The sea is called 'דרך' on its own. The sky is only called 'דרך' when it is tied to the eagle. So the sea stays included and the sky does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is called
Plainly, with no added words

steps.whatToRemember: For שילוח הקן, the sea counts as 'בדרך' because a פסוק calls it a plain 'way'. The sky does not count, because it is only called 'the way of an eagle'.

phrases.english: It is called "the way of an eagle,"
but it is not called simply "a way."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in wording: a plain 'דרך' versus a 'דרך' with an added word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any place a פסוק calls 'דרך' in any form counts, so the sky would be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a place called plain 'דרך' counts. The sea qualifies and the sky does not.

steps.title: A nest on a person's head: what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: The people of פפוניא ask רב מתנה whether a nest found on a person's head needs שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of פפוניא said to רב מתנה: If someone found a nest on a person's head, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: This opens a new topic. A new question about שילוח הקן is asked: does a nest sitting on someone's head count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubt is whether a person's head is like the ground, so the מצוה applies. The other side is that a head is not a normal place for a nest, so maybe it does not apply. The question sets up רב מתנה's answer from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of פפוניא, a town in Babylonia
What is the law?

phrases.english: The people of Pappunya said to Rav Mattana:
If one found a nest on the head of a person,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ פַּפּוּנָאֵי לְרַב מַתְנָה: מָצָא קֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about where שילוח הקן applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a nest on a person's head need שילוח הקן?

steps.title: A head is called 'ground', so the מצוה applies
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה brings the פסוק 'ואדמה על ראשו'. It treats a person's head like ground, so the מצוה applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'And earth upon his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers with a פסוק. Since what is on a person's head is called 'אדמה', the head counts like the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'dust' on his head, but it says 'אדמה' (earth/ground). From this word choice, רב מתנה learns that a head is like the ground. So a nest there needs שילוח הקן.

keyTerms.meaning: Earth or ground
His head

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions just say 'he said'.

phrases.english: "And earth upon his head."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:32. Because a head is spoken of with 'earth' on it, it is treated like the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the מצוה applies, because a פסוק treats a head like 'ground'.

steps.title: The hint to משה in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: Asked where משה is hinted at in the תורה before he was born, רב מתנה points to 'בשגם הוא בשר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is משה hinted at in the תורה? 'For that he also is flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The people of פפוניא keep asking רב מתנה, now about hints in the תורה. He finds משה hinted at in a פסוק from the time of the מבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בשגם' adds up to the same number as 'משה'. The same פסוק goes on to say man's days will be 120 years, which is exactly how long משה lived. So the פסוק hints at משה long before he was born.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is it found (hinted at) in the תורה?
'For that also'; the same number value as משה
Counting the number value of a word's letters

steps.confusionAlert: These are hints (רמזים), not legal sources. רב מתנה is not proving any law here, just showing that these people and events are hinted at in the תורה.

phrases.english: Moses: from where in the Torah?
"For that he also is flesh."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:3. בשגם equals משה in number, and the פסוק continues '120 years', which is how long משה lived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same questioners now turn from הלכה to hints in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is משה hinted at in the תורה?

steps.title: The hint to המן in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: המן is hinted at in the question to אדם הראשון, 'המן העץ', spelled like המן and tied to a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is המן hinted at in the תורה? 'Did you eat from the tree?'
steps.whatsHappening: The next question is about המן. רב מתנה finds his name in the words 'המן העץ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'המן' (from) is spelled with the same letters as the name המן. It appears right next to 'העץ', the tree, which hints that המן ended up hanged on a tree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Did you eat from the tree?', spelled like המן

phrases.english: Haman: from where in the Torah?
"Did you eat from the tree?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:11. המן is spelled the same as המן's name, next to the word 'tree'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is המן hinted at in the תורה?

steps.title: The hint to אסתר in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: אסתר is hinted at in 'ואנכי הסתר אסתיר‎', ה׳ hiding His face.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is אסתר hinted at in the תורה? 'And I will surely hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: The next question is about אסתר. רב מתנה finds her name in the word 'אסתיר', 'I will hide'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אסתיר' sounds like 'אסתר'. The פסוק speaks of ה׳ hiding His face during hard times, which fits the story of אסתר, where ה׳'s name is never openly mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: I will surely hide (My face)

phrases.english: Esther: from where in the Torah?
"And I will surely hide."
phrases.notes: דברים 31:18. אסתיר sounds like אסתר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is אסתר hinted at in the תורה?

steps.title: The hint to מרדכי in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי is hinted at in 'מר דרור', the top spice of the שמן המשחה, which the תרגום renders 'מירא דכיא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is מרדכי hinted at in the תורה? As it is written, 'מר דרור', and we translate it into Aramaic as 'מירא דכיא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The last question in the series is about מרדכי. רב מתנה finds him hinted at through the Aramaic translation of a spice name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מר דרור' is the finest myrrh, the first spice of the anointing oil. Its Aramaic translation, 'מירא דכיא', sounds like 'מרדכי'. This hints at מרדכי's high standing among the Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure flowing myrrh, a spice in the שמן המשחה
We translate it (in the Aramaic תרגום)
Aramaic for 'pure myrrh'; it sounds like מרדכי

steps.whatToRemember: רב מתנה answers both a הלכה question (a head counts as ground for שילוח הקן) and a series of hint questions: משה (בשגם), המן (המן העץ), אסתר (הסתר אסתיר), and מרדכי (מר דרור / מירא דכיא).

phrases.english: Mordecai: from where in the Torah?
As it is written: "Flowing myrrh,"
phrases.notes: שמות 30:23

phrases.english: and we translate it: "Mira dakhya."
phrases.notes: The Aramaic words sound just like the name מרדכי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final question in the series of hints.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is מרדכי hinted at in the תורה?

steps.title: Two ways to say the pigeons' name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about birds that are not ready at hand. Then it brings a disagreement between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון about the right name of the house pigeons mentioned there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Which bird is not ready at hand, etc.' רבי חייא and רבי שמעון disagree. One says the name is הדרסיאות, and the other says הרדסיאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה. It shows two ways of saying the name of a kind of house pigeon. This sets up the next step, which explains each name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody here argues about the הלכה. Both sages agree these pigeons are exempt because they are raised at home. They only disagree about how to read the name in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ready at hand: a bird that already belongs to you or is under your control
One way of saying the name of a kind of house pigeon
The other way of saying the same name

phrases.english: 'And which is one that is not ready at hand, etc.'
Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon:
one teaches 'hadrasiyot',
and one teaches 'hardasiyot'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the hints for מרדכי and the others and goes back to explain a word in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two ways to say the pigeons' name: הדרסיאות and הרדסיאות

steps.title: Where each name comes from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each version. הרדסיאות is named after הורדוס. הדרסיאות is named after the place the pigeons came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says הרדסיאות means they are named after הורדוס. The one who says הדרסיאות means they are named after their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each way of saying the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One name comes from a person, King הורדוס. The other comes from a place. This leads straight into רב כהנא's story about הורדוס's pigeons.

keyTerms.meaning: Named after
King הורדוס (Herod)
Their place, where they came from

phrases.english: The one who teaches 'hardasiyot':
it is named after Herod,
and the one who teaches 'hadrasiyot':
it is named after their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two names given in step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרדסיאות is named after הורדוס, and הדרסיאות is named after the pigeons' place

steps.title: רב כהנא's story of הורדוס's pigeons
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says he saw huge rows of pigeons calling out 'my master'. One pigeon said 'my master, my slave' instead, and it was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I saw them myself. They stood in sixteen rows, each a מיל wide, and called out 'קירי, קירי' (my master, my master). One pigeon did not say it the right way. Its friend said: 'Fool, say קירי קירי!' It answered: 'Fool, say קירי כירי (my master, my slave)!' They took that pigeon and slaughtered it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story, not a הלכה. It backs up the idea that these pigeons were connected to הורדוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pigeons praise הורדוס as their master. The one pigeon that would not join in calls him a slave and gets punished. This fits the tradition that הורדוס began as a slave, so the story makes fun of his claim to be king.

keyTerms.meaning: Rows
The width of a mil, a measure of distance
'My master' (Greek)
Literally 'blind one'; used here to mean 'fool'

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I myself saw them,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; it just stresses 'I myself.'

phrases.english: and they were standing in sixteen rows, each a mil wide,
and they were saying 'my master, my master',
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the words in round brackets. The corrected wording uses the words in square brackets instead. Both mean they were calling out.

phrases.aramaic: (הֲוָה חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ דְּלָא הֲוָה קָרֵי קִירִי קִירִי)
phrases.english: (there was one of them that was not calling out 'my master, my master')
phrases.notes: This line in round brackets is in the printed גמרא. The corrected wording leaves it out and uses the next line instead.

phrases.english: [there was one that did not know how to say it],
its friend said to it:
'Fool, say: my master, my master!'
It said: 'Fool, you say: my master, my slave!'
phrases.notes: Changing just one sound turns the praise into an insult that calls הורדוס a slave.

phrases.english: They brought it and slaughtered it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that supports the link between the pigeons and הורדוס from step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא saw הורדוס's pigeons praising him, and the one that insulted him was slaughtered

steps.title: רבי חנינא's comment: 'words'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רבי חנינא said one word about the story: מילין, 'words'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רבי חנינא told me, 'Words.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי passes on רבי חנינא's short comment about the pigeon story. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what that comment means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, 'words' could mean 'just empty talk', as if the story never happened. That reading is what the גמרא challenges in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Words; this could mean 'just talk'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Rabbi Chanina said to me:
phrases.notes: The word 'רבי' in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: 'Words.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a comment on רב כהנא's story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא described the story with the word 'מילין'

steps.title: Could he really call it empty talk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: can you really think רבי חנינא would call רב כהנא's eyewitness report empty words?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think he said 'just words'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to reading רבי חנינא's comment as 'it never happened'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא said he saw it with his own eyes. It does not make sense that רבי חנינא would brush that off as made up.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? Can you really think so?

phrases.english: 'Words', can that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of רבי חנינא's comment in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי חנינא's 'מילין' as 'just empty talk'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot call an eyewitness report from רב כהנא a made-up story

steps.title: Read it 'through words'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: רבי חנינא said במילין, 'through words'. The pigeons acted this way because of spoken spells.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'through words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes one letter in רבי חנינא's comment. Now he is not saying the story was false. He is saying it really happened, through words of magic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the letter ב changes 'words' into 'through words'. So רבי חנינא agrees the story happened, and he only explains how the pigeons came to talk.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say it this way (the גמרא is fixing the wording)
Through words, meaning words of magic

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי חנינא denied the story. After the correction, he agrees it happened and only explains that it worked through magic words.

phrases.english: Rather, say: 'through words.'
phrases.notes: He means the pigeons acted this way through spoken spells, not that the story was made up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by fixing the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא said the story was just talk
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא said it happened through words of magic

steps.title: Source that a non-kosher bird is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a non-kosher bird is exempt from שילוח הקן. Then it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A non-kosher bird is exempt from sending away.' Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the rule without a reason. The גמרא wants to know which word in the פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird
Exempt from sending away the mother bird
Where do we learn these words? What is the source?

phrases.english: 'A non-kosher bird is exempt from sending away.'
From where do we learn this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the pigeon story and moves to a new rule in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that a non-kosher bird is exempt from שילוח הקן

steps.title: The word צפור means only a kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the פסוק uses the word צפור, not עוף. עוף includes kosher and non-kosher birds, but צפור is only used for kosher birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The פסוק says, 'If a bird's (צפור) nest happens before you.' The word עוף would include both kosher and non-kosher birds. But with צפור, we find that a kosher bird is called צפור. We do not find a non-kosher bird called צפור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by pointing to the exact word the תורה chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had written עוף, every bird would be included. Because it wrote צפור, a word used only for kosher birds, the מצוה applies only to kosher birds. So a non-kosher bird is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird; this word is used only for kosher birds
A bird in general, kosher or not
It means to us; it would include
We have found

steps.whatToRemember: The מצוה of שילוח הקן applies only to kosher birds. We learn this from the word צפור, which the תורה uses only for kosher birds, unlike עוף, which covers all birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of the מצוה in practice: if you find the nest of a non-kosher bird, there is no מצוה to send away the mother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Because the verse says,
'If a bird's nest happens before you',
phrases.notes: דברים 22:6

phrases.english: the word 'of' would mean to us
phrases.notes: He means: had the פסוק used the word עוף, it would have meant...

phrases.english: both kosher and non-kosher.
But 'tzippor':
we have found a kosher bird called 'tzippor',
we have not found a non-kosher bird called 'tzippor'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״כִּי יִקָּרֵא קֵן צִפּוֹר לְפָנֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says צפור, a word used only for kosher birds, instead of עוף, which would include all birds

steps.title: First challenge: the likeness of any winged bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק about not making images, 'the likeness of any winged bird,' to suggest that צפור includes non-kosher birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The likeness of any winged bird.' Isn't it that 'bird' means kosher and non-kosher birds, and 'winged' means grasshoppers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's rule with a פסוק. If צפור there means every kind of bird, then צפור is not only for kosher birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two words, צפור and כנף. The challenge says צפור covers all birds, so כנף must be adding something else, namely grasshoppers. If that reading is right, רבי יצחק's source for exempting a non-kosher bird falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Likeness, an image or form
Wing; here 'winged' creatures
Grasshoppers or locusts
'Is it not that...?' A way of suggesting a reading in order to prove a point

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is asking about images or idols here. The פסוק is only brought for how it uses the word צפור.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"The likeness of any winged bird,"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:17

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו ״צִפּוֹר״ – בֵּין טָהוֹר בֵּין טָמֵא,
phrases.english: is it not that "bird" means both kosher and non-kosher,
and "winged" means grasshoppers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's claim in step 27 that צפור only means kosher birds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that צפור only refers to kosher birds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this פסוק צפור seems to include all birds, with כנף adding grasshoppers. So צפור can mean non-kosher birds too.

steps.title: Answer: bird means kosher, winged means non-kosher and grasshoppers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading: צפור is kosher birds, and כנף covers non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Bird' means kosher birds, and 'winged' means non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק by splitting the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words are still needed, but they divide the work in a new way. צפור stays limited to kosher birds, and כנף picks up both non-kosher birds and grasshoppers. So the פסוק does not prove that צפור includes non-kosher birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher (here, a kosher bird)
Non-kosher (here, a non-kosher bird)

phrases.english: No, "bird" means a kosher bird,
and "winged" means non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the words split the categories differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צפור covers all birds and כנף means grasshoppers.
steps.terutzMaskana: צפור means kosher birds only, and כנף covers non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.

steps.title: Second challenge: animals, creeping things, and winged birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים listing creatures that praise ה׳, again suggesting צפור includes all birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The wild animal and all domestic animals, creeping things and winged birds.' Isn't it that 'bird' means kosher and non-kosher, and 'winged' means grasshoppers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again with a different פסוק that also says צפור כנף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is a list of all kinds of creatures, so it seems to want every bird included under צפור. The challenge is the same: then כנף must mean grasshoppers, and צפור includes non-kosher birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild, undomesticated animal
A domesticated animal
Creeping things

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"The wild animal and all domestic animals,
creeping things and winged birds,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 148:10

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו ״צִפּוֹר״ – בֵּין טָהוֹר בֵּין טָמֵא,
phrases.english: is it not that "bird" means both kosher and non-kosher,
and "winged" means grasshoppers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יצחק, built the same way as step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that צפור only refers to kosher birds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full list of creatures should include all birds under צפור, leaving כנף for grasshoppers.

steps.title: Same answer for the פסוק in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: צפור is kosher birds, and כנף is non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Bird' means kosher birds, and 'winged' means non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers this challenge exactly like the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list still includes every creature, because כנף covers the non-kosher birds. So nothing forces צפור itself to include non-kosher birds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Winged bird'; read here as two separate groups

phrases.english: No, "bird" means a kosher bird,
and "winged" means non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 using the same split as step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צפור in the list covers all birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: צפור means kosher birds, and כנף covers non-kosher birds and grasshoppers.

steps.title: Third challenge: every bird of every wing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק about the animals entering נח's ark and asks the same question again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Every bird of every wing.' Isn't this the same challenge we raised before?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third פסוק and doesn't repeat the whole argument. It just says 'like we challenged before.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is the same as in steps 28 and 30. צפור would mean all birds and כנף would mean grasshoppers, so צפור would include non-kosher birds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we challenged', meaning the same challenge as before

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"Every bird of every wing,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:14

phrases.english: is it not as we challenged?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that צפור only refers to kosher birds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same as before: צפור would cover all birds, with כנף meaning grasshoppers.

steps.title: Answer: as we answered before

steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is as we answered.

steps.deeperAnalysis: צפור is kosher birds, and כנף covers non-kosher birds and grasshoppers. Since the פסוק fits that reading, it proves nothing against רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Fourth challenge: speak to the bird of every wing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from יחזקאל, 'Speak to the bird of every wing,' and raises the same challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And you, son of man, speak to the bird of every wing.' Isn't this the same challenge we raised before?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last פסוק and again says only 'like we challenged before.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same: if צפור here means all birds, then רבי יצחק is wrong that צפור is only for kosher birds.

steps.title: Answer: as we answered before, and רבי יצחק's rule stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the last challenge the same way, so רבי יצחק's reading holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is as we answered.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Every time צפור appears next to כנף, the גמרא reads צפור as kosher birds and כנף as non-kosher birds and grasshoppers. None of the four פסוקים forces צפור to include non-kosher birds.

steps.whatToRemember: Four פסוקים were brought to show that צפור includes non-kosher birds. All four were answered the same way: צפור means kosher birds, and כנף covers non-kosher birds and grasshoppers. So רבי יצחק's source for exempting a non-kosher bird from שילוח הקן still stands.

phrases.english: No, it is as we answered.

steps.title: Opening another source to test the reading

steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 28 through 35 brought four challenges, and each was answered the same way: צִפּוֹר is a kosher bird, and כָּנָף includes non-kosher birds and grasshoppers. Here the גמרא opens a fresh attempt. The actual source and the challenge come on the next amud.
